claims.text: A predictive approach that explicitly represents atomic-level disorder will accurately identify HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity.
Lattice distortions and local chemical inhomogeneities enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Accounting for atomic-scale fluctuations will produce intrinsic lattice-thermal-conductivity predictions at least 20–30% lower than conventional-model predictions.
The target HfNbTaTiZr material can be prepared as a single-phase, low-impurity alloy with a homogeneous microstructure.
The cited processing route can produce nearly fully densified equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Temperatures above 800 °C are relevant operating conditions for the proposed thermal-insulation application.
Atomic-scale disorder and lattice distortions in a single-phase HEA matrix mediate phonon scattering.
The random distribution of multiple principal elements causes strong damping of lattice vibrations.
Representing disorder-related scattering centers allows the approach to identify alloys with substantially reduced phonon transport.
Active or passive lattice filling with a low-conductivity aerogel is a relevant atomic-scale scattering effect in the proposed HEA system.
Experimental measurements will show a thermal-conductivity reduction commensurate with the predicted 20–30% decrease.
Conventional predictive models neglect detailed atomic-disorder effects.
The predictive approach is primarily applicable to single-phase HEAs with uniform microstructures and controlled impurity levels.
Secondary oxides, precipitates, or multiple phases may reduce prediction accuracy because they alter phonon scattering independently of alloy chemistry.
Thermal conductivity can be derived from laser-flash thermal diffusivity together with heat capacity and density measurements.
Failure to observe at least a 20% reduction relative to conventional predictions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism introduces low-conductivity aerogel filling in the lattice core, whereas the rest of the hypothesis specifies a homogeneous, single-phase HEA and excludes secondary phases; an aerogel-filled material would ordinarily be a distinct composite architecture.

The hypothesis and predicted outcome quantify a 20–30% decrease in predicted conductivity, while the uncertainty field calls the same percentage an improvement in prediction accuracy. Lower predicted values and greater predictive accuracy are different metrics.
